recommended_substrate_queue_entry.title: ContextMemory.write() hard-argmin addressing has a deterministic single-slot fixed point under a low-variance query stream -- give the WRITE path the non-degenerate selection the READ path already has
recommended_substrate_queue_entry.implementation_hint: ContextMemory.read() (ree_core/predictors/e1_deep.py:124-133) addresses by softmax over query_proj(query) @ key_proj(memory).T, but ContextMemory.write() (lines 135-147) addresses by a hard scores.mean(0).argmin(), which under a near-constant query stream is a deterministic single-slot fixed point -- established at 436e by a closed-form sign discriminator q . (write_signal - memory[argmin]) that predicted lock-vs-rotate 5/5. Primary build: apply the annealed Gumbel-softmax selection that V3-EXQ-908 ALREADY CONFIRMED works (3/3, genuine context-conditioned sparsification) to the WRITE address, or add an occupancy/usage-balancing term so the fixed point cannot form. Note compute_diversification_loss() already acts on self.memory but the write update runs under torch.no_grad() and is unaffected by it. Secondary/complementary lever (NOT this entry): raise z_world entropy via the SD-070 encoder recipe so the query stream stops being near-constant. This is the WRITE-side sibling of substrate_queue SD-016, which is scoped to cue-indexed RETRIEVAL and is already `implemented`; an amend there would misfile it.
recommended_substrate_queue_entry.priority_rationale: One fresh failure record (V3-EXQ-436f), and it blocks 3 claims -- either arm of the governance Step 6a-ii.6 rule gives priority 1.
recommended_substrate_queue_entry.severity_rationale: Every ContextMemory consumer writing under a low-variance query stream silently gets a 1-slot bank while write() returns normally and thousands of calls are logged. Nothing errors, the readout is well-formed, and the resulting null looks like a genuine 'sleep has no effect' finding. That is the definition of `corrupting` -- evidence that LOOKS valid but is not -- and it has now produced exactly that artefact twice (436e, 436f). Classified by what the defect does to evidence quality, not by fix difficulty.

biological_reference.divergence: LOAD-BEARING, on the credit rule specifically. Standard extinction theory requires an unreinforced EMISSION of the response to weaken it, not its mere non-occurrence. Charging decay on every freeze/no-op tick -- which under sustained threat vastly outnumber directed attempts (70-188:1 measured here) -- is not extinction, it is a tick-count artefact. The environment/pressure shortfall, by contrast, is a divergence of the TEST BED from the reference paradigm, not of the mechanism's translation.

cluster_pattern.parent_grouping_verdict: PARTLY CONFIRMED. The surface fingerprint the parent session grouped on is real and correctly observed. But the proximate causes are TWO INDEPENDENT BUGS sitting at OPPOSITE ENDS of the measurement pipeline, over ONE shared structural property at the substrate layer. They are NOT one structural property at the level of proximate cause, and a fix for either does nothing for the other.
cluster_pattern.why_two_bugs_not_one: V3-EXQ-436f's occupancy shortfall is a collapse of the INDEPENDENT VARIABLE -- the manipulation had nothing to act on and the discrimination statistic was mathematically UNDEFINED on 3 of 5 seeds. V3-EXQ-603u's headroom shortfall is a saturation of the DEPENDENT VARIABLE -- the manipulation may well have acted, the statistic WAS computed, but the ruler had no range left (7 of 9 arm-seeds pegged at the 200-step cap). One is 'nothing to measure'; the other is 'the ruler is pegged'. They need two independent builds with no shared component: a write-address selection mechanism in ree_core/predictors/e1_deep.py, and an eligibility-trace credit/decay rebalance in ree_core/pfc/infralimbic_avoidance_gate.py (already in flight).
cluster_pattern.substrate_ceiling_fingerprint_applies_to: V3-EXQ-603u ONLY. The skill's 'negative control passes, discrimination fails' tell fits 603u cleanly (LESION passed at 1.0, the discrimination failed). It does NOT fit V3-EXQ-436f, where the discrimination was never COMPUTABLE, not computed-and-null. Reading 436f through that fingerprint would misdescribe it -- which is why 436f's failed_criterion is recorded as readiness_precondition and 603u's as discrimination.
cluster_pattern.structural_property: In BOTH cases the REE substrate instantiates the mechanism's STRUCTURE while failing to sustain the DYNAMIC RANGE the mechanism's readout requires. ContextMemory has 16 slots and 2,837-4,903 write calls per arm and occupies 1. The ilPFC gate logs 31,000-35,000 updates and 405 credit events and holds an efficacy of 1e-120. Both pass every liveness/engagement check that counts EVENTS; both are functionally absent on the MAGNITUDE that matters. This is 'symbol of the mechanism, not its functional role' specifically at the level of magnitude, and it is invisible to any readiness check built from counters.
cluster_pattern.second_shared_property_positive: Both drivers carried a PRE-REGISTERED two-sided guard (436f: sd016_arming_engaged vs sufficient_occupancy_for_c1; 603u: LESION-below plus POSCTRL-above), and in both cases the guard fired correctly and REFUSED to score a vacuous comparison rather than emitting a false claim-layer verdict. Both FAILs are informative refusals. This is a methodological maturity signal in the lineages and is the reason both runs are non_contributory rather than spurious `weakens`.
cluster_pattern.planning_decision_forced: Do NOT treat these as one gap with one fix. Two independent builds are required. The one thing they DO share is a cheap, generalisable methodological repair worth adopting across the corpus: liveness/engagement preconditions must be evaluated over the SCORING WINDOW and on MAGNITUDES, not as whole-run EVENT COUNTS. Both runs would have self-reported their true state one gate earlier had they done so.
